components.css: .ds-dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 62px minmax(0, 1fr) 90px auto; gap: 10px; align-items: center; width: 100%; border: 0; border-top: 1px dotted var(--line-2, #d5cfe0); border-radius: 0; background: none; padding: 5px 10px; text-align: left; font: 400 12.5px/1.3 var(--ui, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif); color: var(--ink, #111); cursor: pointer; } .ds-dl:hover { background: var(--fill-2, #faf8fc); } .ds-dl:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--lilac-deep, #6a3fa8); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-days { font: 700 30px/0.9 Bahnschrift, 'DIN Alternate', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; text-align: right; } .ds-hot { color: var(--lilac-deep, #6a3fa8); } .ds-days small { display: block; font: 600 11px var(--ui, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif); color: var(--mute, #5c5866); margin-top: 3px; } .ds-main { min-width: 0; } .ds-t { display: block; font-weight: 700; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-s { display: block; font-size: 12px; color: var(--mute, #5c5866); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-date { font: 700 14px Bahnschrift, 'DIN Alternate', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; text-align: right; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip { font: 700 11px/1.3 var(--ui, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif); padding: 1px 6px; border: 1px solid; border-radius: 2px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-dark { color: #fff; border-color: var(--ink, #111); background: var(--ink, #111); }

narrative.overview:
Scholarship Desk is a high-density mosaic in the Japanese web-portal tradition (catalog world `japanese-high-density-web`, chosen by the user; seed `ab41c36ee743b8e1`). Everything the applicant must know and do sits on one screen as a grid of hairline-ruled rectangular modules: next deadlines, what needs them, pipeline and fit, documents, drafts, what is coming up, and the full list. Nothing floats, nothing is padded for air. Information is the decoration.

The palette is **lilac, white and black**, the user's choice on 2026-11-12, replacing the original utility red. Lilac owns the shell as fields: the top bar, the tab strip and every module header. Black carries text, the active tab, module tabs and decided tags. Deep lilac is the single accent that carries text and urgency: days-left figures, notes, urgent tags and focus. Numbers are set like prices in a DIN-style face so the eye can scan figures down a column. Text is the platform UI sans at 12 to 13px with tight leading.

The system runs under hard constraints that are part of its identity: system font stacks only (the user declined self-hosting a web font on 2026-11-12), a CSP of `default-src 'self'` (no external fonts, no inline styles), DOM built with `textContent`, and no build step. There is no dark theme: the background is always white, whatever the system setting (the user's choice, 2026-11-12).
keyCharacteristics: 12-column mosaic of bordered modules with 8px gutters, everything above the fold on desktop.
Lilac shell: lilac top bar, light lilac tab strip and module header bars, each module headed by a black tab at its left edge.
Heavy tabular DIN-style numerals for days left, counts, dates and KPIs, in deep lilac when urgent.
Three colours only: lilac, white, black. Status lives in outlined tags; only black (decided) and deep lilac (urgent) fill.
2px corners, 1px hairlines, dotted row separators, zero shadows.

rules.name: The Three-Colour Rule
rules.body: Lilac, white and black, nothing else. Lilac is a field (bar, strip, header); black is text and decisions; deep lilac is the only accent and marks urgency and focus. Never add a hue for status.

rules.name: The Outline-Only Status Rule
rules.body: States appear as text with a 1px outline on the panel colour. The only filled tags are ink (decided) and deep lilac (urgent).

rules.name: The Price Figure Rule
rules.body: Every figure the applicant scans (days left, counts, dates, word counts) is set in the numeral face at 700 with tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is on `body`). Words never use the numeral face.

rules.name: The Two-Step Size Rule
rules.body: Body copy lives between 11px and 15px. Size contrast comes from the 30px numerals, not from big headings.

rules.name: The Above-the-Fold Rule
rules.body: On a desktop viewport the Overview shows deadlines, needs, pipeline/fit, documents and drafts without scrolling. A new module earns its place by being scannable at this density.

rules.name: The Hairline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px line or a tone step, never a shadow or blur.

dos: Do put every new block of information in a module: Lilac Mist bar, black left tab, title, optional deep-lilac numeral note, "View all" link.
Do set every scannable figure in the numeral face (Bahnschrift / DIN Alternate) at 700 with tabular figures.
Do express status with the tag grammar: outlined for a state, ink filled for decided, deep lilac filled for urgent.
Do keep rows on one line with an ellipsis before the figure column, separated by 1px dotted rules.
Do define every colour as a token on `:root`; there is one (light) theme.
Do keep fonts to system stacks and all styles in `styles.css` (CSP `default-src 'self'`, no inline styles, no build step).
donts: Don't introduce any hue beyond lilac, white and black (red, green, blue, ochre are retired).
Don't put white text on light lilac; lilac fields always carry black text.
Don't add a dark theme or follow the system's dark mode; the background stays white (the user's choice, 2026-11-12).
Don't add shadows, blur or floating cards; separation is hairlines and tone.
Don't load external or self-hosted web fonts; the user declined them on 2026-11-12.
Don't spread the Overview into airy stat cards with large padding; the mosaic is meant to be packed.
